title: Kissed Smoky Middle Eastern Lamb Tagine
description: A charred and cozy Middle Eastern dish featuring tamarind pulp and smoky flavors, this lamb tagine is a hearty and flavorful meal, friendly to those with egg allergies. The combination of tender lamb, sweet and sour tamarind, and aromatic spices creates a deliciously complex flavor profile.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in the bottom of a clay or ceramic tagine or a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the lamb pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the tamarind pulp, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil.
Cover the tagine or Dutch oven and transfer it to the oven, where it will cook at 300 degrees Fahrenheit for 2 1/2 hours.
Remove the tagine from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving.
Serve the lamb and sauce over couscous or rice, garnished with fresh parsley or cilantro.
Refrigerate or freeze any leftovers for later use.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
